blocks.text: Neuland Laboratories is a Hyderabad-based manufacturer of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and advanced intermediates. It does not make finished formulations [F] (AR2026 p.8). It earns money in two ways. **Custom Manufacturing Solutions (CMS)** is contract development and manufacturing of new-chemical-entity APIs and intermediates for innovator companies, run on an exclusive basis per project [F] (AR2026 p.5, p.10). **Generic Drug Substances (GDS)** splits into Prime (large-volume, mature, contested molecules such as Mirtazapine and Ezetimibe) and Specialty (low-volume, complex molecules such as Apixaban, Donepezil, and Paliperidone and Aripiprazole sterile) [F] (AR2026 p.8, p.82). The company reports a single segment, 'manufacture of active pharmaceutical ingredients and allied services', so its statutory accounts disclose no segment revenue or margin [F] (AR2026 p.196).

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. **Valuation far above every scenario in our DCF model.** The price is Rs 21,505 against bear / base / bull values of Rs 2,080 / 3,308 / 4,435 per share. The reverse DCF implies ~83.5% five-year sales CAGR against a base-case equivalent of 13.6% [E] (NUMBERS).

2. **Concentration.** Management says commercial CMS 'is being driven by a handful of molecules… maybe about 3' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The top 5 CMS products are 94% of CMS revenue [F] (RATING). Three customer groups each exceed 10% of revenue, together ~54% [E] from [F] (AR2026 p.196).

3. **The quality of FY26 cash flow depends on customer advances.** Advances from customers rose from Rs 72.6 cr to Rs 244.5 cr [F] (AR2026 p.190). Excluding the Rs 173.9 cr working-capital inflow from other liabilities, FY26 CFO of Rs 346.7 cr would have been ~Rs 173 cr, or ~0.48x PAT [E] (AR2026 p.176).

4. **Working capital swelled.** Receivables rose from Rs 315.7 cr to Rs 541.4 cr and inventories from Rs 385.8 cr to Rs 510.3 cr in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.175). The company's own cash conversion cycle went from 107 to 137 days [F] (AR2026 p.83).

5. **FY26 margins were helped by FX, and the size is not quantified.** 'Favourable foreign exchange movements also contributed meaningfully' [F] (AR2026 p.14). Management itself points investors to a 25% EBITDA anchor, against 35.5% in Q1 FY27 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Forex gain in other income was Rs 10.6 cr vs Rs 0.6 cr [F] (AR2026 p.191).

6. **Capex intensity is rising ahead of contracts.** FY26 capex was Rs 397 cr, 68% of EBITDA [E] (NUMBERS). Approved capex totals Rs 1,460 cr over 13 quarters [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), plus a Rs 126 cr purchase of 134 acres at Kakinada [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS). Peptide work has 'no firm contracts because these are early-stage projects' [MC] (CALL May 2026). FY26 FCF was -Rs 50 cr [F] (NUMBERS).

7. **GDS is shrinking.** Prime fell 5% and Specialty 16% in FY26 [F] (RATING). Paliperidone shipments were hit by customer-side issues, with resolution pushed to 'next financial year' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

8. **Disclosure is thin, and there are candour questions.** No order book, segment margins or product revenue are disclosed. CMS molecule names are withheld under confidentiality [MC] (CALL May 2026). An investor alleged that the Q3 FY26 transcript was altered; the CFO said that on checking there was 'no change in this section' [MC] (CALL May 2026; CALL Aug 2026).

9. **Promoter pay rose faster than profit.** The three promoter whole-time directors received Rs 42.3 cr in FY26, up 37-46% each, against PAT growth of 40% [E] from [F] (AR2026 p.120, p.114). Promoter holding is only 32.62% [F] (NUMBERS).

10. **Single-region manufacturing.** All three plants and R&D are around Hyderabad, Telangana [F] (AR2026 p.127). One regulatory event at a site making a top CMS molecule could remove a large share of profit [AI].

**Is TTM a new base or a peak?** Bull view: Q4 FY26 plus Q1 FY27 sales of Rs 1,418 cr show the run-rate has stepped up [F] (NUMBERS). Bear view: management calls Q4 'exceptionally inflated… a Q3 plus Q4 kind of a performance' and declines to call Q1 a base [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

**Margin durability.** Bull view: Q1 FY27 gross margin was 61.2% with CMS-led mix [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Bear view: management guides only '25% plus' and credits exchange rates [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Our DCF base case uses 29% [F] (NUMBERS).

**Peptides.** The market may be over-crediting this: there are no firm contracts, and management describes the peptide business as potentially 'another Neuland' that 'may take more than a few years' [MC] (CALL May 2026). The market may also be under-crediting it if one commercial peptide NCE lands in FY27, which the CEO called the 'ideal' outcome [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

**Pipeline replenishment.** Commercial CMS molecules have held at 19 for at least three years (Q1 FY24, Q1 FY26 and Q1 FY27) [F] (PPT Aug 2026). Bulls point to larger value per molecule; bears point to stagnant counts [AI].

**What the reverse DCF actually says.** Our model uses a 15% WACC [F] (NUMBERS). Even if the cost of capital is too high, the gap between Rs 4,435 (bull) and Rs 21,505 is too large for discount-rate tweaks to close within the sensitivity grid (max Rs 4,415 at 13.5% WACC / 6.5% g) [E] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus narrative is a high-quality Indian CDMO at the start of a peptide-led growth phase. Our differentiated read is that FY26-Q1 FY27 earnings rest on about three commercial CMS molecules, with a favourable FX tailwind and a sharp build in customer advances flattering cash flow. Meanwhile the capital base is being doubled through capex that is not yet contracted. The business quality is real: regulatory track record, exclusive CMS projects, rising gross margin. But at 55x TTM earnings and 36.6x EV/EBITDA [F] (NUMBERS), the price already assumes the pipeline converts at scale. The asymmetric risk is a molecule-specific setback, such as a customer change of control (management did not comment when asked about Esperion's acquisition) [MC] (CALL May 2026), rather than a slow erosion.

[AI] The company is 42 years old, but the business that drives today's valuation is recent. CMS was '10%, 15% of our total revenues' about 5-7 years ago [MC] (CALL May 2026) and was 43% in FY25 and 61% in FY26 [F] (RATING). Unit III only became productive in 2021, and its new 52 KL block was commissioned in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.12, p.42). Commercial-scale peptides date from about 2024 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The long history therefore supports the regulatory track record more than the earnings profile, which has only two strong years (FY24 and FY26) separated by a down year (FY25) [F] (NUMBERS).

3. **Scale-up and clinical supply.** The company manufactures quantities for Phase 1-3 trials; launch quantities are classified as development revenue [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
